clue.text: Streak of light reveals nothing in the meter

indicators.note: the clue puts nothing in the meter, so the round letter goes inside that word

parts.note: the word meter itself, with the 'the' carried along in the surface
O looks like zero

explanation.surface: A flash of light seems to show that a measuring gauge reads zero.
explanation.definitionFit: A shooting star is seen as a brief bright trail across the night sky.

clue.text: Contemptible Desmond has Greek letter put on telegram

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece put on another sits above it, so the Greek letter comes before the telegram

parts.note: DES is a common short form of the name Desmond
pi is the Greek letter
a cable is an old word for a telegram sent by wire

explanation.surface: A man called Desmond is scorned for sending a telegram with a Greek symbol on it.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe something deserving scorn or utter disdain.

clue.text: Intelligence ensnares horrible hound in mystery

indicators.note: to ensnare is to trap something inside, so the jumbled hound sits within the word for intelligence

parts.note: wit means quick intelligence

indicators.note: something horrible is mangled out of shape, so the letters of hound are rearranged

parts.note: the word hound supplies the letters to be jumbled

explanation.surface: A clever mind traps a dreadful dog, as in a detective tale like The Hound of the Baskervilles.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is the informal name for a detective story, usually spelt here with one N.
explanation.definitionFit: A mystery is a detective novel or play in which a crime puzzle is solved.

clue.text: Cushion will start sagging regularly

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter, here the opening letter of sagging

parts.note: the word sagging, whose first letter is taken
often means frequently, at regular intervals

explanation.surface: A cushion is predicted to begin drooping at regular intervals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Regularly' looks like an instruction to take alternate letters, but it simply gives a synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: To cushion a blow is to lessen or deaden its impact, a verb sense.

clue.text: Be quiet about a preference, like a spitfire

parts.note: sh is the sound used to hush someone
re means concerning, as in a letter heading
a wish is something one would prefer

explanation.surface: Someone is told to keep quiet about liking the Spitfire fighter plane.
explanation.walkthrough: A spitfire here is not the aircraft but a fiery, quick-tempered person.
explanation.definitionFit: A shrew is a bad-tempered scolding woman, so the adjective describes a hot-tempered spitfire.

clue.text: Programme presenter to face husband

parts.note: to front something is to face it
man as in man and wife

explanation.surface: A TV host has to confront a husband.
explanation.definitionFit: A frontman is the person who hosts a show and appears before the cameras.

clue.text: Left silly grey hat behind, showing sluggishness

indicators.note: the jumbled grey hat comes behind, that is after, the letter for left
silly suggests nonsense, so the letters of grey hat are rearranged

parts.note: the words grey hat supply the letters to be jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone abandoned a foolish grey hat, a sign of their lazy mood.
explanation.definitionFit: Lethargy is a lack of energy, the same dull slowness as sluggishness.

clue.text: To trump is cruel by the sound of it

indicators.note: the word for cruel is heard, not spelt, so its sound gives the answer

parts.note: rough treatment is harsh or cruel

explanation.surface: Playing a trump card is said to be an unkind move.
explanation.definitionFit: In card games such as bridge, to ruff is to play a trump card on another suit.

clue.text: Scream suppressed by Mary Ellen

indicators.note: the answer is held down inside the name Mary Ellen, across the gap between the words

parts.note: the name runs the letters together: marY ELLen

explanation.surface: Mary Ellen stifled a scream.
explanation.definitionFit: A yell is a loud cry, much the same as a scream.

clue.text: Having run wild, Ted goes to Rio

indicators.note: Ted goes to Rio, so his name is attached after the city's

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Ted went wild on a trip to Rio de Janeiro.
explanation.definitionFit: To riot is to behave in a violent, unruly way, so having rioted is having run wild.

clue.text: Saint Paul has included definition in this piece of garden!

indicators.note: St Paul includes the abbreviation within his letters, so it sits inside them

parts.note: taken as written
def is a standard short form of definition

explanation.surface: A gardener named Paul has added a dictionary entry to his plot.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is loose: a spadeful is as much of the garden's soil as one spade lifts.
explanation.definitionFit: A spadeful is the amount of earth lifted on a spade, a piece of the garden.

clue.text: Form of irrigation wanting care when repaired

indicators.note: to repair is to put back together, so the letters of wanting care are rebuilt

parts.note: the words wanting care supply all eleven letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: An irrigation device needs attention once it has been mended.
explanation.definitionFit: This garden can sprinkles water on plants, a simple means of irrigating them.

clue.text: Broadcaster's reward seen to be dreadful

definitions.note: the definition is broadcaster; the 's is a contracted 'is' linking it to the wordplay

indicators.note: something dreadful is in a bad state, so the letters of reward seen are jumbled

parts.note: the words reward seen supply the ten letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A broadcaster's payment is judged to be awful.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who reads the news on radio or TV is a kind of broadcaster.

clue.text: Required result: nothing wanted in the highest seats

indicators.note: nothing is wanted in, that is let inside, the highest seats

parts.note: the gods are the topmost seats in a theatre balcony
O looks like zero

explanation.surface: The desired outcome: nobody wanted in the cheap seats at the top of a theatre.
explanation.walkthrough: The gods is the theatre name for the highest, cheapest gallery.
explanation.definitionFit: To deliver the goods is an idiom for producing what was promised or needed.

clue.text: Ancestor regretted standing up for pomp

parts.note: a gran is a grandmother, one of your forebears

indicators.note: in a down clue a word standing up is read from bottom to top, so regretted's synonym is reversed

parts.note: rued means felt sorry for

explanation.surface: An ancestor's regret at defending pomp and ceremony.
explanation.definitionFit: Grandeur is splendour and magnificence, the stately display that pomp describes.

clue.text: Trivial display taking everyone in

indicators.note: the display takes the word for everyone inside it
completes taking in, meaning holding within

parts.note: a show is a display
all means everyone

explanation.surface: A showy but empty spectacle that draws in everybody.
explanation.definitionFit: Shallow means lacking depth or seriousness, much like trivial.

clue.text: Drink offering disturbed lion a bit

indicators.note: disturbed means upset or thrown into disorder, so the letters of lion a bit are rearranged

parts.note: the words lion a bit supply the eight letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A drink offered to a lion annoyed it somewhat.
explanation.definitionFit: A libation is wine or another drink poured out as an offering to a god.

clue.text: Murderer, taking slow boat back, caught her

indicators.note: back means the word for the slow boat is read in reverse

parts.note: a tub is a clumsy, slow-moving boat
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
taken as written

explanation.surface: A killer catches a woman by taking an old boat back to her.
explanation.definitionFit: A butcher is figuratively a brutal killer who slaughters people.

clue.text: Music-maker's container made of wood and newspaper?

definitions.note: the definition is music-maker; the 's is a contracted 'is' linking it to the wordplay

parts.note: a barrel is a wooden cask
an organ is a publication speaking for a group, such as a party newspaper

explanation.surface: Asking what an instrument's case is made of: wood and newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: A barrel organ is the hand-cranked street instrument played by organ grinders.
explanation.definitionFit: A barrel organ produces tunes mechanically when its handle is turned, so it is a music-maker.

clue.text: Sooner of later a single person needs time

definitions.note: printed this way, but the phrase is 'sooner or later'

parts.note: one stands for a single person, as in 'one can only try'
a day is a period of time

explanation.surface: Eventually, a lone individual needs some time to themselves.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition reads 'Sooner of later' in the source; 'sooner or later' is meant.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying something will happen one day means it will happen at some point eventually.

clue.text: Check cold in sanatorium

indicators.note: cold is placed in the short form of sanatorium

parts.note: san is a short form of sanatorium, a convalescent hospital

explanation.surface: A doctor checks for a cold in a hospital ward.
explanation.definitionFit: To scan is to examine or look over something closely.

clue.text: Retreat from PM having lost original letter

indicators.note: the prime minister's surname loses a letter, so it is taken out of the name

parts.note: Tony Blair was a British Prime Minister
the original letter of the surname is its first one

explanation.surface: A refuge away from the Prime Minister, who has mislaid a first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A lair is a hideaway or den, a place to retreat to.

clue.text: It's nonsense to applaud deception

parts.note: to clap is to applaud
a trap is a trick or ruse

explanation.surface: Clapping a con trick is rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: Claptrap is empty, pretentious talk, which is drivel.

clue.text: Aloof TV controller?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: distant and standoffish in manner
second meaning: the handheld device for changing channels

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark hints that an aloof person might be pictured as someone controlling the television.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both emotionally distant and the zapper that operates a set from the sofa.

clue.text: Tapered dart is stuck into little Edward

indicators.note: a dart is stuck into Ned, so the word for dart goes inside his name

parts.note: Ned is a pet form of Edward
an arrow is a dart

explanation.surface: A pointed dart has hit young Edward.
explanation.definitionFit: Something narrowed has become thinner towards one end, which is what tapered means.

clue.text: Her saw cut up a rope

indicators.note: cut up means chopped into pieces, so the letters of her saw are reassembled

parts.note: the words her saw supply the six letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A woman uses a saw to cut through a rope.
explanation.definitionFit: A hawser is a thick cable used for mooring or towing ships.
